evidence.source: Academia Sinica, 漢字字形演變資料庫
evidence.text: The entry says 到 is formed from 人 and 至, with 人至 expressing arrival; in the small-seal form, 人 was transformed into a phonetic 刀, yielding 至 as semantic and 刀 as phonetic. This is the database’s analysis; the page does not demonstrate a dated transition or establish that the change was corruption.
evidence.title: 漢字「到」：字形演變

evidence.source: Ministry of Education, Taiwan, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.field: Shuowen analysis, reading, senses, and paleographic availability
evidence.text: The entry records 說文釋形 ‘至也。从至，刀聲’, Mandarin dào, and senses including ‘arrive/reach’ with 詩經·大雅·韓奕 ‘靡國不到’, ‘thorough/complete’, and ‘go to’. Its listed oracle-bone and bronze reference collections are marked unavailable, so this page does not verify those glyphs.
evidence.title: A00348 到 — Ministry of Education Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants

evidence.source: Baxter and Sagart, Old Chinese: A New Reconstruction project page
evidence.text: The authors’ page identifies its downloadable Old Chinese lists as supplementary materials for their 2014 book. The supplied local Baxter–Sagart table has separate rows for 刀 (MC taw; OC *C.tˤaw), 到 (MC tawH; OC *tˤaw[k]-s), and 至 (MC tsyijH; OC *ti[t]-s). These checked local rows support a close 刀–到 syllable-shape comparison within Baxter–Sagart’s system, while their distinct suffixes and tone categories remain distinct. Local row provenance: sources/baxter-sagart/baxtersagart.tsv, records 刀, 到, 至; the external project page was inspected, but no character-specific upstream PDF table row was inspected in this invocation.
evidence.title: The Baxter-Sagart reconstruction of Old Chinese

evidence.text: Checked supplied local rows: 刀 dāo, 到 dào, 至 zhì. Local provenance: sources/unihan/Unihan_Readings.txt, kMandarin rows 刀, 到, 至. These are current reading metadata, not evidence for an ancient sound relationship. search_audit.outcome: Search did not surface the requested official Unihan record or exact Commons page in an inspectable form. It returned the Unicode code chart for U+5230 and search-result-only text for the Wikibooks file description. No image provenance or reuse rights were established.

gaps: The exact 到-seal.svg Commons page and upload.wikimedia.org SVG both returned cache-miss errors; the exact Commons imageinfo API lookup was inaccessible, and the Wikibooks file page also failed. The supplied local copy was not downloaded or pixel-inspected here. Its literal identity, provenance, script-period basis, and reuse rights therefore remain unverified, so it cannot be selected.

The local Unihan kMandarin rows were checked, but the required official Unicode Unihan records for 刀, 到, and 至 could not be opened. Their local readings are not externally verified click-through evidence in this result.

Baxter–Sagart local rows were checked for all three characters, but the character-specific entries were not read from the authors’ external PDF during this invocation. The authors’ project page verifies the dataset’s provenance and system context, not those individual forms.

The sources support both the Shuowen-style 至+刀 analysis and Academia Sinica’s account of 人+至 developing into a phonosemantic graph. The precise graphic transition and chronology, and whether any corruption occurred, remain unresolved. The Taiwan MOE entry’s listed oracle-bone and bronze collections are unavailable; no securely dated earliest inscription was established.

The received 詩經 example gives an early literary use glossed as ‘arrive/reach’, but this research did not establish the wording’s composition or transmission date. The other reported senses’ dates and semantic pathways remain unresolved.
